newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Philip Morris wins Portugal's Tabaqueira.
newsitem.headline: Philip Morris wins Portugal's Tabaqueira.

text.p: U.S. firm Philip Morris on Thursday won the bidding for a controlling stake in Portugal's state-owned Tabaqueira tobacco concern.
The company will pay some 33 billion escudos ($210 million) for the 65 percent holding the Socialist government was offering as part of its privatisation programme.

In an alliance with Portuguese group Jorge Mello, it fought off competition from a consortium led by Spain's Tabacalera and French company Sieta (Ste Nationale d'Exploitation Industrielle des Tabacs et Allumettes).

Although its offer was slightly below that of Tabacalera, the government had said all along that price would not be the only consideration and that it would also be looking at the candidates' plans for the industrial development of the sector.
The decision on the sale of the stake, taken at a cabinet meeting on Thursday, came after the country's competition watchdog, the Competition Council, had given the green light to all three bids.
The government sought the Council's opinion because Tabaueira holds a dominant position in the Portuguese market with some 70 percent of sales.
Philip Morris was already the country's second largest supplier and the takeover will lift its share of Portuguese cigarette sales to around 90 percent.

It has pledged to create 100 new jobs and boost Portuguese cigarette output to 21 billion by 2001 from 10 billion now. Tabaqueira was the last big privatisation of 1996 with the government having comfortably exceeded its $2.5 billion revenue target from sales. ($1=156.97 escudos)
